column1: # constexpr.tsv -- C values of the Oberon-07 constant expressions the
# front end's folder folds (oberon/src/const_eval.rs).  Written by
# constexpr.c, which computes every value with the runtime helpers the
# back end emits (rt_div, rt_mod, rt_lsl, rt_asr, rt_ror, rt_set, rt_in,
# rt_floor, rt_flt, rt_ord) -- no literal values, no other algorithm.
# Format: one data row per expression, `<expression><TAB><decimal value>`.
# Values: INTEGER/BOOLEAN/CHAR are signed decimal (two's complement for
# 32-bit patterns); SET is the 32-bit pattern as an unsigned decimal;
#  * `-7 DIV 3` is `-(7 DIV 3)`, the report's grammar binds a leading
#    sign to the whole term (DESIGN 8.3), so it is NOT (-7) DIV 3; the
#    parenthesised rows carry the negative-dividend cases.
#  * `7 DIV -3` / `7 MOD -3` are not grammatical (no sign on a factor),
#    so the negative divisor is spelled `(0 - 3)`.
#  * `~{0}` is absent: unary `~` needs a BOOLEAN operand (report 8.2.1)
#    and the folder rejects it; a SET complement is written `-{0}`.
#  * integer `/` is the folder's documented DIV (see const_eval.rs);
#    `(0 - 7) / 3` is the row that discriminates it from C's truncated `/`.
